messages:
Alex: Hey team, AcmeCorp reported a big burst this morning — they started getting 429s from their private customer-managed gateway. They say it was a short CI blast. From our side the initial signs point to quota exhaustion at the gateway token-bucket, but they also have ingress limits in k8s so need help triaging which limiter fired and why. Full context below.

Priya (AcmeCorp): We kicked off a bulk embedding job — roughly 1200 concurrent requests over ~30s. We didn't change any Redwood config. We observed per-key 429s and intermittent 5xxs. We need a short writeup for our postmortem.

Alex: Gateway log slice we captured: 
```
[2026-03-14T10:12:04Z] INFO request_id=abcd1234 route=/v1/embeddings status=429 reason=\"token_quota_exceeded\" key=proj-acme-01
[2026-03-14T10:12:04Z] WARN ratelimiter=global bucket_tokens=0 burst=50 last_refill=2026-03-14T10:11:35Z
```

Maria (SRE): Can you paste their gateway rate-limiter config and the ingress annotations? Need to check if Envoy local limits and our control-plane quotas overlapped. Also confirm this is customer-managed gateway (VPC) with Envoy running in their cluster?

Alex: They confirmed customer-managed, Envoy in k8s. Their provided snippets: 
```
# ingress excerpt
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rate: \"0\"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: \"200\"
    envoy.ingress.kong.io/rate-limit: \"true\"
spec: ...
```
and their gateway config (customer-facing):
```
rate_limiter:
  type: token_bucket
  capacity: 500
  refill_tokens: 50
  refill_interval_ms: 1000
  per_api_key: true
  burst: 250
```

Simon (Eng-runtime): A few notes: with refill=50/sec and burst=250, a sustained 1200-concurrency blast will exhaust many per-key buckets fast. Also our control plane has short-window per-key safety quotas that can surface 429s as "token_quota_exceeded". To determine which component returned the 429 check response headers — look for our gateway header (x-rw-gateway-error) vs Envoy local header (x-envoy-ratelimited).

Priya (AcmeCorp): We reproduced in staging with this command: 
```
hey -n 1200 -c 1200 -m POST "https://private-gw.acme.example/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxx" -d '{"input":"long text..."}'
```
Response headers we captured: `x-rw-gateway-error: token_quota_exceeded` on many responses, and `x-envoy-ratelimited: \"true\"` on others.

Maria (SRE): That header combo strongly suggests both the Envoy local limiter and our gateway quota enforcement fired for different requests. Hypothesis: initial burst tripped Envoy local limits, and as aggregate requests continued our control-plane short-window quotas also started rejecting.

Simon: Can you pull envoy admin stats from the pod? Example: `curl -s http://localhost:9901/stats | grep rate_limit` — look for counters like `ratelimit.over_limit` and `local_ratelimit.enforced`. If they use a shared datastore (Redis) for rate-limit state, collect those counters too.

Alex: Customer returned these numbers: envoy stats show `ratelimit.over_limit: 1274` and `local_ratelimit.enforced: 1200`. Our control-plane logs show `proj-acme-01 throttle_window=1s count=1203`.

Maria (SRE): Ok that lines up. Short-term recommendations to customer: 1) reduce concurrency, or 2) temporarily raise token bucket/refill and burst to allow the job to complete, and 3) use backoff/retry jitter on the client so concurrent workers don't sync. For longer-term: recommend per-worker API keys or increase per-key capacity for CI jobs.

Simon: Operational notes — if per_api_key=true and they reuse the same key across many parallel processes, they'll collide on the same token bucket. If they can issue per-worker keys (even short-lived), parallelism won't hit a single bucket. Also consider connection-based limiting at the ingress layer (limit-connections) for this workload instead of strict req/sec limits.

Priya (AcmeCorp): We were reusing a single project key for the whole CI matrix. Rotating keys per worker is possible but we'd prefer platform-level smoothing so occasional blasts don't hard-fail.

Maria (SRE): For debugging we asked them to collect these artifacts next time: 
- `kubectl get pods -n gateway -o wide` and envoy pod name
- `kubectl logs <envoy-pod> --since=15m | grep rate_limit`
- `curl -s http://<envoy-pod-ip>:9901/stats | grep rate_limit`
- control-plane throttle logs (we pulled these already)
- optional pcap of egress if networking anomalies suspected

Alex: Suggested a recommended config we can add to docs (shared as a draft for review):
```
# Redwood suggested token-bucket for high-concurrency embed jobs
rate_limiter:
  type: token_bucket
  per_api_key: true
  capacity: 2000
  refill_tokens: 400
  refill_interval_ms: 1000
  burst: 800
# k8s ingress recommendations
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: \"200\"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm: \"0\"  # disable naive rpm limits for bursty workloads
```

Simon: I'll file an internal runtime enhancement to add short-window smoothing heuristics that detect single-key floods and apply transient queuing/smoothing instead of immediately escalating to quota errors (ENG-8294). That should reduce customer interruptions for short blasts.

Maria (SRE): Immediate operational steps taken: we applied a 1-hour soft quota bump for acct-proj-acme-01 so they could finish the job. Billing team confirmed no invoice impact for the temporary bump.

BillingBot: Auto-note: soft-quota increase applied for proj-acme-01 for 1 hour. Reverts at 2026-03-14T12:30:00Z.

Priya (AcmeCorp): Running a smaller test at 300 concurrent now — looks stable, thanks. :thumbsup:

Alex: Action items: 
- Simon: open ENG-8294 (runtime smoothing heuristic)
- Maria: update private-gateway docs with recommended token-bucket profiles and ingress guidance (DOC-441)
- Priya: try per-worker keys and request a config review if needed

Priya (AcmeCorp): We'll follow up if we hit the limits again. Appreciate fast help :raised_hands:

Maria (SRE): Marking thread resolved. If they see 429s again we'll ask for envoy admin dump + pcap, and reopen.

oncall-bot: Deployed gateway config v2026.03.12 to private clusters at 2026-03-12T03:23:00Z

Alex: Closing loop — Priya confirmed the run finished and we reverted the soft-bump. Saved logs in the incident folder in case we need to reopen.
